PLAN AUDIT: Potomac Pulse flood replay (2026-10-12→19). All times are UTC. USGS dateTimes carry -04:00 (EDT), and I converted them to UTC.

Evidence scripts (read-only, run by me):
- /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-sebjilke/252f7c3c-5965-4854-a165-14468fc066da/scratchpad/pulse-audit/out/plan-audit/check_latency.py
- /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-sebjilke/252f7c3c-5965-4854-a165-14468fc066da/scratchpad/pulse-audit/out/plan-audit/check_ceiling_lag.py
- /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-sebjilke/252f7c3c-5965-4854-a165-14468fc066da/scratchpad/pulse-audit/out/plan-audit/check_inforce_correction.py

Verdict: the plan's main problem is the rule "latest USGS values at or before the tick". That rule leaks future readings into the replay. Two other gaps matter as much. The fidelity gate covers almost no rising-limb rows, and the corrected pass uses bins that already contain learning from the flood. The six traces also replay the server cron's estimate. During the flood, paddlers mostly saw a different estimate, computed in their browser.

AMENDMENTS (the replay builder and analysts MUST follow these)

1. Freeze the clock. makeGFPrediction never takes a "now" argument. It reads Date.now() in getPoRFromHistory, getPoRRiseRateFromHistory, getFlowState and validationDue. The replay must stub Date.now() to each tick's run time:
   - Rows that exist: use the row's created_at minus about 2 s. Cron rows land at HH:00:15–HH:00:27.
   - Synthetic ticks: use HH:00:20.
   Restore the clock after each call.

2. Model USGS reporting latency. Do not feed "the latest value at or before the tick".
   - Evidence: at three ticks, the actualCFS and actualStage the cron recorded match current USGS values 65–80 min before validatedAt, and both match at the same lag. The ticks are 10-14T09 (20,100 cfs), 10-14T21 and 10-15T09.
   - At 10-14T09 the newest value now on file for that time is 21,400 cfs. The cron had 20,100, which is 6% lower.
   - The 10-14T06 and 10-14T09 rows hit the ceiling. Dividing their predicted values by 1.2 gives the LF the cron saw: 17,400 and 20,100. 20,100 is about 70 min old (script: check_ceiling_lag.py). 17,400 appears in the record only 10 min before the tick, while the newest value at the tick is 17,600.
   - At flat flow the lag cannot be identified (repeated values), so treat it as unobserved there.
   - Required approach: apply a per-gauge lag L (the cron's view = readings with time ≤ tick − L). Fit L against the fidelity rows. Report the results at L = 0, 15, 30, 60 and 75 min. Never report only the zero-lag replay.

3. Lag every input from the same "available-at-tick" set:
   - lf.q
   - por.q
   - the PoR history tail
   - Monocacy and Goose (15-min series)
   - Broad Run and Seneca
   - the Edwards Ferry stage (15-min)
   - water temperature
   Stale tails change several things together: the rise rate (current = last history entry, so its time span is shorter than 6 h), the wave-celerity cut to travel time (capped at 30% once the rise reaches 15%/h), the convergence of the travel-time iteration, flowState (por.q against the last reading at or before now−6h), the EF weight, the >50% EF discrepancy skip, and the 120%-of-LF ceiling, which uses the stale lf.q.

4. Build PoR history the way storePoRHistory does:
   - Use the union of the P2D fetches made at all earlier hourly ticks.
   - Keep the first value seen for each timestamp. A later USGS revision never overwrites a stored value.
   - Keep readings newer than tick − 72h. Drop readings with cfs ≤ 0 or ≥ 500,000.
   - The replay cannot see original-versus-revised PoR values. The por-history endpoint keeps only 72h, so those values are gone. Say so; do not assume no revisions.

5. Water temperature has no effect on this event, and the replay must not invent one:
   - PoR temperature ran 13.9–21.7 °C from 10-08 to 10-21, so the cold EF model (≤10 °C) never applies. Pass the PoR 00010 latest value at the tick.
   - The LF 00010 series in the data file is empty.
   - waterTempC is absent from every October hard-flag row. That field arrived in v37.21.

6. Flag reproduction must use v37.20 rules, not the frozen v37.21 code. v37.21 shipped 2026-11-09, after the flood. Under v37.21 the Check-3 ice gate (UTC months 10, 11, 0–2 = Nov–Mar, or temperature ≤5 °C) would not flag October. Under v37.20, the four pre-event LOW_FLOW_HIGH_STAGE rows (predictions 10-07T11 → 10-09T17) were hard-flagged. The validator diff must be stated.

7. Score two kinds of "truth" and keep them separate:
   - App truth: what the app scored. That is lf.q at the first hourly tick at or after validationDue, within 2.5 h. That value is itself up to about 80 min stale, as in amendment 2.
   - Physical truth: LF interpolated at validationDue from the current USGS record.
   Use app truth for the fidelity gate and when reproducing published accuracy. Use physical truth for skill findings. Report the gap between them.

8. Widen the fidelity gate. The planned gate (rawPredictedCFS on the October hard-flag rows) covers the 10-11T12 row before the rise, the 10-14T06 and 10-14T09 rows (both clipped at the ceiling), and the falling limb from 10-14T18 to 10-18T01. It has no raw row on the rising limb (10-12T02 → 10-14T06). Add three checks:
   - (a) Validation timing for every stored prediction. Interleave hard-flag and clean rows. A prediction is created at the tick where the previous one was validated, because the cron validates and then stores in the same run. The replayed validationDue must fall in the interval (validated tick − 1 h, validated tick].
   - (b) Corrected values for clean rows, but only where the bins are known (amendment 10).
   - (c) The ceiling-implied LF on the two clipped rows.
   Report a match table for each check.

9. Handle validation timing exactly. validationDue = run time + travelGFtoLF. That travel time uses the multiplier from the iteration, and on a rising river that multiplier comes from the low historic PoR flow, not today's LF. This likely explains the long rising-limb gaps (10-12T02→T15, 13 h; 10-12T15→10-13T07, 16 h). The replay must reproduce the 3-step iteration, the <1 h convergence break and the 1 h match window in selectHistoricReading. It must not compute travel time from the current LF.

10. Split the corrected pass at 10-15T16Z. The 10-15T16Z bin snapshot already contains flood learning (12000-25000 rising: 7 obs; 25000-50000: 59 obs).
    - Before 10-15T16Z: present the corrected values only as "approximate, contaminated with learning from the flood itself". Bracket them between empty bins and the 10-15 bins.
    - From 10-15T16Z on: build bins exactly. Start from the 10-15 snapshot and apply the logged updates: 12000-25000 falling → (24, 81) from the 10-15T20 validation, and 6000-12000 steady 1→5 from 10-18T13 to 10-19T10. Run updateCorrectionBin in time order.
    - Check: with the 10-19 values, the C45-interpolated correction reproduces raw − predicted on every hard-flag row from 10-16T00 to 10-18T01 to within 1 cfs (188, 290, 378, 401…; script: check_inforce_correction.py).
    - Use the 10-11T12 row (155, identical in both snapshots) as a check on the bins before the event.

11. Use the observed in-force corrections as ground truth. On rows not clipped by the ceiling, the correction in force equals rawPredictedCFS − predictedCFS. Before 10-15T16 these values differ from the snapshot: 12000-25000 falling was 209 at 10-14T18 and 403 at 10-15T06, against 230 in the snapshot. The analysis must report this difference and must not overwrite those values with snapshot values.

12. The two ceiling rows can say nothing about the correction. At 10-14T06 and 10-14T09 the "implied" values (6,655 and 3,900) are mostly the 120%-of-LF clip. Report ceiling binding separately, against the stale lf.q.

13. Model the single pending slot explicitly:
    - The hourly replay gives two outputs: (i) the server's hourly predictedCFS, which fed the gf_history graph line (24 h retention, now gone), and (ii) the stored and validated subsample, about one prediction per travel time.
    - Learning and accuracy come only from (ii). Report how many hourly predictions were never scored. Report how much of the rising limb (10-11T12 → 10-12T15) passed while the slot was locked.

14. Check row origin before using any row in the gate. A gf_prediction 'pending' row can also come from the API path: sync-learning.js action storePrediction. That path writes a reduced field set and no porEstimateCFS. Accept only rows created at HH:00:1x–:00:3x (cron) and exclude the rest. All October rows passed this check.

15. Treat hard-flag censoring as an outcome. STATISTICAL_OUTLIER (Check 5, z-score against the bin's cumulative meanError and SD) hard-flagged 16 of the 18 rows from 10-14T06 to 10-18T01. Check 5 alone flagged 15 of them. Hard flags remove a row from learning and from avgErrorPercent. avgErrorPercent barely moved (7.379 → 7.3755 from 10-15T16 to 10-19T16), while hard flags went from 40 to 52. The headline accuracy figure excluded most of the falling limb, and analysts must report that.

16. Check 5 depends on bin state at the moment of validation (count, sumError, sumErrorSq), and that state was not captured. Do not claim to reproduce a flag decision. Use the anomalyFlags as logged.

17. Advisory replay must keep state. The EF divergence and LF residual advisories (updateEfDivergenceState / updateLfResidualState in model.js) carry state from tick to tick, and the LF residual one takes validation pairs as input. Replay them as a chain, not one tick at a time. Check the replay against the ef_divergence_episode and lf_residual_episode rows in Supabase.

18. Every finding must cite the replay's lag setting and fidelity-match result. A trace finding that rests on a replay window where the fidelity gate failed must be labelled UNVERIFIABLE.

THREATS TO VALIDITY (state these in the final report)

- **Latency is uncertain.** The cron's actual view of USGS at each tick was never logged except in three places: lf.q/h at validation, and lfCFS on the ceiling rows. PoR, tributary and EF latency are not observable and are inferred only through replay fit.
- **Provisional revisions.**
  - LF values at the event's validation ticks still match the cron's values (as of today's file), so there is no evidence of LF revision at those 23 points.
  - PoR, tributary and EF revisions cannot be checked. The stored first-seen PoR history is gone.
  - Monocacy carries 'A' (approved) for 10-04T23Z–10-07T14:30Z, so those values may have been edited. That window is before the event.
- **Bins before 10-15T16Z are unknown.** The corrected-pass results before then carry leakage from the flood's own learning.
- **The gate is small and lopsided.** About 18 raw rows from the event, almost all from the peak or falling limb. Rising-limb raw fidelity rests on validation-timing checks and clean corrected rows only.
- **Validation definition.** The app validates the GF estimate against raw Little Falls discharge, including the ungauged area below GF, and does so at hourly ticks with stale LF. "Error" means error against LF as the app sampled it. It is not error against Great Falls.
- **One event, about 39 scored predictions.** Most hourly predictions were never scored, and the stored ones were picked by the slot-lock timing, not at random. These are observations, not skill estimates.
- **Code version.** The estimator is identical to v37.20, but the validator differs (Check-3 gate). Flag provenance must be stated per amendment 6.
- **Bin-state source.** The 10-15 and 10-19 bin values come from a capture by an earlier review session. The 10-19 bin values are recorded only as two "changes".
- **Unlogged run failures.** Cron cadence was continuous from about 10-07T21 to 10-19T16 (consecutiveRuns 188 → 285, missedRuns flat at 655). A run that threw before updateRunHealth would count as missed, so that part is covered. A run where the USGS fetch succeeded but makeGFPrediction returned null (LF or PoR missing) would not show up anywhere.

WHAT THE SIX TRACES WOULD MISS

1. **What paddlers actually saw.**
   - The page shows a browser-side estimate: estimateGreatFalls in src/estimation/great-falls.js.
   - It uses its own data: a P7D/P1D client fetch, localStorage PoR history, a median-robust rise rate (a deliberate divergence from the server) and an NWS fallback for flow state.
   - The server replay does not reproduce this number. Only the gf_history graph line was server-side.
2. **The 48h forecast is sampled only when someone views the page.** gf_forecast_pending rows are written only by browsers, through storeForecastPredictions on page render. Forecast-counter changes over the event reflect when someone had the page open, not hourly coverage. Per-row forecasts and NWS inputs are gone.
3. **Stage learning.** The stage_* bins, avgStageErrorClean and stageObsClean, and the displayed stage against the LF rating breakpoints (estimateLFStage).
4. **Server shadow models and the shadow_leaderboard.** These are stateful and fed by the raw estimate.
5. **The CI band.** The client's getGFUncertainty takes the bin SD from the sync API, and bins with few observations behave oddly: 12000-25000 steady had n=1 with ema 9,743, which then blends with the fallback at weight 1/5.
6. **Pre-event false ice flags.** v37.20 hard-flagged four October low-flow validations as ice (LOW_FLOW_HIGH_STAGE). This was fixed only in v37.21.
7. **Other UI and plumbing.** Creeks UI, map, gauges UI, offline banner, Sentry/healthchecks behaviour, staleness or caching in the sync-learning endpoints, and the soft-flag counter frozen at 165 from 10-15 to 11-09. That counter freeze needs a check: either nothing was soft-flagged, or the counter path is broken.

The replay dataset is built and its fidelity gate passes: the chosen latency setting reproduces all 20 logged raw estimates within 1%. The lag fit and the gate use the same rows, so the match is in-sample. On the rising limb (10-11T12 to 10-14T06) no raw estimate was logged, so those replayed raw values are unverified.

**Outputs** (all in `/private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-sebjilke/252f7c3c-5965-4854-a165-14468fc066da/scratchpad/pulse-audit/out/replay/`):
- `replay_hourly.csv`: 313 ticks, 80 columns, chosen lag setting.
- `replay_hourly_L0.csv`, `replay_hourly_L15.csv`, `replay_hourly_L30.csv`, `replay_hourly_L60.csv`, `replay_hourly_L75.csv`: same dataset at a uniform lag on every gauge, no overrides.
- `replay_build.cjs`: CommonJS; imports the real `makeGFPrediction`, `fetchUSGSData`, `fetchWaterTemp` and `getPoRFromHistory` from `_test`, plus the `shared/model.js` helpers. Fetch and Supabase are stubbed; nothing loads from the live repo.
- `fidelity_table.csv`, `fidelity_table_lag_sensitivity.csv`, `fidelity_summary_by_lag.csv`.
- `REPLAY_NOTES.md`: column dictionary, reconstruction rules, rerun commands, caveats.
- Supporting: `best_lags.json`, `fit_trace.csv`, `grid_fit.csv`, `lf_lag_scan.csv`, `lf_overrides.csv`, `exactbins_updates.json`, `phase_summary.csv`, `phase_by_lag.txt` (from `phase_by_lag.py`), `advisory_compare.txt` (from `compare_advisories.py`), `supabase_episodes_2026-10.json`.

**Lag setting** (minutes): PoR 55, LF 10, Monocacy 5, Goose 5, Broad Run 50, Seneca 20, Edwards Ferry 45. LF has per-tick overrides of 70/65/70 min at 10-14T09, 10-14T21 and 10-15T09, where the logged LF value proves an older reading. Six lags were fitted on 22 constraints. Per amendment 18, each finding should cite the lag setting and the tick's `fidelity_evidence` value.

**Fidelity** (41 logged rows: 20 hard-flag, 21 clean, 10-08 to 10-19):

| Check | Chosen setting | Uniform L=0 | Uniform L=60 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw vs `rawPredictedCFS` (n=20): median / max abs diff | 0.15% / 0.83% | 0.74% / 9.1% | 0.18% / 2.2% |
| Raw within 2% | 20/20 | 17/20 | 18/20 |
| Ceiling-implied LF values reproduced (of 8) | 8 | 1 | 0 |

At the chosen setting, all of these also match:
- **Bin-implied raw on clean rows:** within 0.31% and 0.15%.
- **Logged cron LF values:** all 39 `actualCFS` and all 8 ceiling-implied values exact.
- **Validation timing:** 41/41 replayed `validationDue` fall in the observed interval.
- **Flow state and bin:** 41/41 each.
- **Corrected values from 10-15T16 on:** 17/17 within 0.57% using reconstructed bins. In-force corrections match within 4 cfs.
- **Pending-slot chain:** reproduces all 41 observed prediction-creation ticks.
- **LF-residual advisory stamps:** match every row.
- **Edwards Ferry divergence:** ratio within 0.009 median. The replay misses 4 logged one-tick deactivations, probably Edwards Ferry readings older than 2 h, which cannot be observed.

**Phase summary** (all hourly ticks, chosen lag; error vs Little Falls interpolated at `validationDue`; MAPE / bias). "Approx-corrected" uses the 10-15T16Z bin snapshot at every tick, so it already contains learning from the flood.

| Phase | Ticks | Raw | Approx-corrected |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pre (10-08 to 10-11) | 72 | 12.0% / +11.0% | 8.2% / −3.5% |
| Onset (10-11T00 to 10-12T00) | 24 | 46.0% / −31.1% | 50.8% / −50.8% |
| Rise (10-12T00 to 10-14T06) | 54 | 23.4% / +23.2% | 11.4% / −7.0% |
| Peak (10-14T06 to 10-15T00) | 18 | 11.5% / +11.5% | 3.9% / +3.9% |
| Recession (10-15 to 10-21) | 145 | 4.5% / −4.3% | 8.7% / −8.6% |

- With the reconstructed bins (10-15T16 to 10-19T16 only, 97 ticks), recession is 9.3% / −9.1%.
- Across all lag settings these phase numbers move by about 2 points at most.
- The app's own scoring value differs from the interpolated Little Falls value by 0.9% mean absolute, up to +17% at the onset.

**Caveats analysts must respect:**
1. Rising-limb raw values are unverified, with up to 45 h to the nearest verified raw. The evidence there is timing, the cron's LF view, and ceiling binding: all 6 clean rising-limb rows were clipped at 1.2 × stale LF, which shows the cron's LF reading but not the raw estimate.
2. The lag fit is in-sample. Late deliveries were observed only for LF. Check findings against the uniform-lag files.
3. Approx-corrected before 10-15T16 is a bracket, not what was displayed. Logged in-force corrections differ from the snapshot (209 and 403 vs 230). Clean rows 10-13T07 and 10-13T14 were ceiling-bound in production but not in the approx pass. Only `exactbins_*` (10-15T16 to 10-19T16) is reconstructed, and its intermediate 6000-12000 steady values come from the replay (error sum −740 vs −816 logged).
4. On the rise, what the app displayed was mostly the 120%-of-LF ceiling on a reading up to 70 min old. Ceiling binding is in separate columns and says nothing about the correction.
5. This is the server cron's estimate only. The browser estimate paddlers saw is not replayed.
6. 47 of 313 hourly predictions were stored, so 266 were never scored; 41 are verified up to 10-19T10. The slot was locked for 24 hourly ticks from 10-11T13 to 10-12T14, covering most of the onset surge.
7. Hard flags come from the log, not reproduced. Flag provenance follows v37.20 rules.
8. Revisions to Point of Rocks, tributary and Edwards Ferry data cannot be checked. Little Falls values at the 39 validation ticks still match what the cron saw.
9. Truth is Little Falls, including ungauged inflow below Great Falls. The onset error is dominated by local runoff: Little Falls reached about 11,500 cfs while Point of Rocks was about 3,000. This is one event, so these are observations, not skill estimates.
10. The Supabase query was SELECT only (the two advisory-episode row types). I made no other network calls, did not touch the live repo, and committed nothing.

AUDIT COMPLETENESS CRITIC: Potomac Pulse flood, 2026-10-12 to 10-19 (times UTC; error = estimate − actual; this is one event, so these are observations, not skill estimates)

I made no Supabase queries, did not touch the live repo, and committed nothing. Wherever I use replay values, they are from the chosen lag setting (por55/lf10/mono5/goose5/br50/sen20/ef45 plus LF overrides). The fidelity caveats are the replay's own; see contradiction C2 for the rising limb.

=====================================================================
1. WHAT NOBODY TRACED (app surface vs aspects)
=====================================================================

Great Falls tab
- The browser estimate (estimateGreatFalls) was never replayed. E8 compared only the rise rate, and its displayed-value claims were not re-checked.
- The Inputs panel and its data-source line were not traced, for example "PoR (45h ago) [Δ-corrected 130%] + 39% EF → LF in ~13 hrs".
- The "FORECAST (no history yet)" path was not traced.
- The gf_history graph was not traced. It comes from client localStorage plus dropLocalSpikes(frac 0.40), and recordGFEstimate stamps entries with render time, not reading time.
- The EF cross-check row (agreement icon) was not traced.
- **Offline service worker and staleness label: not traced. I investigated it (G1 below).**

Creeks tab (creeks-ui.js, CREEK_RUNS)
- Nobody looked at it. I investigated it (G2, and G3 for Difficult Run).

All Gauges tab (gauges-ui.js)
- Only the travel-time column was traced (H4).
- Not traced: NWS flood-category rings (nws.js fetchFloodCategory), per-gauge trend arrows, the ice-flag display, and per-gauge popups.

Map (map.js)
- Not traced. It uses static geojson plus tile layers and is low relevance.

- Nobody checked what it displayed during the event: accuracy, bins, validation tables, shadow leaderboard.
- L8 and OPS-05 cover the underlying numbers but not the display.

- Not traced: the stage_* bins, avgStageErrorClean and stageObsClean, which PLAN listed as missed item 3.
- D6 covered only the rating curve.

- Not traced. OPS-05 covered only the server leaderboard.

- Not traced.

Not traced and not observable to this audit:

- The offline banner.

=====================================================================
2. GAPS INVESTIGATED
=====================================================================

G1. The service worker serves stale USGS data labelled as fresh. HIGH. Single-source: the mechanism is read from code and the effect is simulated.

Code (frozen v37.21; the service worker shipped in v37.10 on 06-23, so it was live during the flood):
- vite.config.js sets StaleWhileRevalidate on `waterservices.usgs.gov|corsproxy|allorigins|api.water.noaa.gov` (cache pp-data, maxAge 6 h).
- fetch.js:386 uses a constant URL (period=P7D), so every fetch hits the same cache key.
- When a cached entry exists, the service worker returns it and refreshes the cache in the background.
- fetchUSGS then calls setLastFetchTime(Date.now()) and sets dataSource "live" (fetch.js:398-399).
- updateStalenessDisplay (fetch.js:544-578) shows "Updated just now" from the fetch time, not the USGS reading dateTime.

Effects:
- A returning visitor first sees data from their previous visit, up to 6 h old, labelled fresh, for up to 15 min (the refresh interval).
- After that, every render is one fetch cycle (15 min) behind, on top of USGS latency.
- The sync-learning bins and advisories are cached the same way (pp-api, 24 h TTL). The advisory freshness guards (2 h) partly protect the banners.
- TODO #19 itself lists the in-browser check of this behaviour as a "pending manual gap".

Effect size, with the server replay standing in for the browser (c1_sw_staleness.txt):
- LF 6 h stale vs current LF: onset mean −20.5% (worst −62%), rise −11.0% (worst −30.8%), peak −12.4% (worst −31.2%). The largest deficit was −7,000 cfs at 10-14T10.
- Displayed estimate (approx-corrected) rendered 6 h late vs truth for tick t:
  - onset MAPE 50.8 → 66.6
  - rise 11.4 → 19.0 (bias −7.0 → −17.1)
  - peak 3.9 → 14.4
  - recession 8.7 → 6.9 (stale happens to help on the fall)
- 1 h stale: onset worst shift −27%. 15 min: up to −5.8% on LF at onset.
- The 120% ceiling is computed client-side from the same stale LF, so on the rise the cap was stale too.

How many paddlers saw stale data is not observable: no browser telemetry exists.

Recommendation:
- Switch the USGS and NWS routes to NetworkFirst with a timeout, or add a cache-buster.
- Drive "Updated …" from the newest reading dateTime.
- Set dataSource from the response's actual freshness.

G2. The Creeks tab has no upper or flood threshold. MEDIUM, safety wording. Single-source.

Code:
- CREEK_RUNS (constants.js:114-119) defines only `runnable`.
- creeks-ui.js:263-264 shows "Running! (≥N cfs)" with a green glow, and the banner says "CREEKS ARE RUNNING", for any q ≥ runnable.

Live USGS (c2_creeks.txt):
- Difficult Run peaked at 1,620 cfs at 10-11T18:45, 8.1× its threshold. It was ≥5× threshold for 6.8 h.
- Rock Creek peaked at 978 (2.4×), NW Branch at 322 (1.6×), Sligo at 556 (2.8×).

During the flash-flood peak, the tab told paddlers these Class III-V creeks were "Running!" in green, with no high-water warning. Whether 8× is above the safe upper limit for Difficult Run is not checked here; American Whitewater ranges are outside the allowlist.

G3. Most of the onset "local runoff" is Difficult Run, which the app already fetches. HIGH for interpreting accuracy. Single-source, but it explains a verified number.

Difficult Run (01646000) joins the Potomac between Great Falls and Little Falls. Its flow is therefore inside the LF "truth" but can never be in a GF estimate.

Comparison with the verified H5 residual (c3_difficult_run.txt):

| Time | H5 residual | Difficult Run excess over baseline |
|---|---|---|
| 10-11T15Z | +756 | +793 |
| 10-11T16Z | +1,638 | +1,171 |
| 10-11T17Z | +2,201 | +1,431 |
| 10-11T18Z | +2,110 | +1,561 |
| 10-11T19Z | +2,193 | +1,581 |
| 10-11T20Z | +2,204 | +1,481 |
| 10-11T21Z | +1,566 | +1,291 |
| 10-11T22Z | +759 | +1,011 |

So Difficult Run alone accounts for about 65-100% of the "unexplained" residual.

At the onset ticks' validationDue:
- Difficult Run averaged 686 cfs, 12.0% of mean truth (max 1,590).
- Scoring against LF minus Difficult Run moves raw onset MAPE from 46.0% to 39.4% and bias from −31.1% to −21.9%.

Consequences:
- The app scores and learns Great Falls error against inflow that enters below Great Falls.
- That inflow was measured and fetched (creeks tab), but never subtracted.
- It contaminates every validation during local storms, the low-flow bins included.

Recommendation: subtract Difficult Run (and an ungauged-area scaling) from the LF truth at validation, or at least flag validations where Difficult Run is above some fraction of LF.

=====================================================================
3. CONTRADICTIONS AND VERDICTS THAT LOOK TOO GENEROUS OR TOO HARSH
=====================================================================

C1. Onset cause.
- Positions held:
  - The replay notes say "dominated by local runoff".
  - E5 (verified CONFIRMED) says "mostly unforecastable local runoff".
  - H5 (CORRECTED) says gauged-tributary timing dominates, with about 2k cfs of ungauged runoff for about 6 h.
  - D3-verify says the worst onset misses were "local runoff".
- G3 shows the "ungauged" part is mostly Difficult Run, which is gauged.
- E5's CONFIRMED is too generous. The onset error mixes horizon (E5 itself: 46.0 → 29.8 at +3 h), tributary timing (H5/H6), and below-GF inflow that is measurable (G3). It should read CORRECTED.

C2. Rising-limb raw fidelity.
- The replay builder says the gate passes 20/20.
- L6 (verified CONFIRMED) shows a failed hard constraint: the n=1 bin (sumErrorSq = 9,743²) forces raw = 20,743 at the 10-12T15 tick. The replay has 16,401 (−20.9%) at every lag setting.
- At that tick the travel time was 45.4 h, the maximum (OPS-08), and the iteration had not converged. That is exactly where a different first-seen PoR history would swing the lookback. This is a plausible cause, not a tested one.
- E1, E2, D3 and the replay "Rise" row (23.4% / +23.2%) were verified as reproductions of the replay, not as true production raw. Under amendment 18, every rising-limb raw magnitude should carry an UNVERIFIABLE label, and the E1 verdict omits that label.

C3. Ceiling binding: raw vs corrected.
- E2-verify additional finding 2 says "the gf_history line on the rise was mostly 1.2×LF (46/54)". L2's 62/72 is the same raw-binding measure.
- OPS-03-verify shows 46/54 is raw binding. Corrected (displayed) binding with the 10-15 bins is 27/54, and true production binding is not observable hourly.
- E2's extra claim is too strong. Only the 8 stored rows are proven clipped.

C4. Advisory timing.
- L3 says the banner was "12 h late". L7 and D4-verify show it was already up 10-11T12 to 10-12T00 for the wrong reason.
- The verifiers caught this, but L3 should be cited only in its corrected form: about 2.5 h of real gain, plus removing a 2-h lapse.

C5. CI mechanism.
- D1 blames the tiny learned bin SD. D1-verify shows the band uses only the fixed backtest q05/q95; stdDev is never rendered.
- The verifier is right. Drop D1's SD recommendation.

C6. Recession bias attribution. E6, L1 and D1/D5 each treat the recession under-read as having one cause. It has two stacked causes:
- The PoR-delta pushes raw down: raw −4.3%, and without the delta −0.6% (E6).
- The frozen +401 bin subtracts on top of that: corrected −9.1% (L1, exact bins).
E6-verify rightly rejected "the delta feeds the corrected miss". The report should present raw recession bias as delta-driven and the extra about −5 pp as bin-driven.

C7. D6 inconsistency left open.
- scheduled-update.js:898 stores predictedStage as the corrected stage.
- Yet 21/21 failure-row stages equal the raw stage.
- D6-verify noted this but marked CONFIRMED with "holds for this file". It is an unexplained export/storage discrepancy and should be an open OPS item, not closed.

C8. E3 vs H8.
- E3 is CONFIRMED with "missing attenuation" as the PoR-route cause.
- H8-verify adds water-supply withdrawals and rating bias as equal candidates.
- E3's recommendation (an attenuation term) rests on an inseparable attribution. CONFIRMED is fair on the numbers but generous on the cause.

C9. Display relevance of the peak over-read.
- E3/E4 rank the +31-37% peak raw over-read as high.
- The displayed values on those rows were ceiling-clipped: 20,880 displayed vs 20,937 truth.
- For users the peak over-read was mostly invisible. It mattered for learning, via the 25000-50000 and 12000-25000 rising bins (L2, L6). Severity for display is too high.

C10. Forecast persistence cross-check (F2). The verifier was correct and the analyst's reproduction was an artifact. No further issue.

C11. Network allowlist.
- The forecast analyst made GETs to api.water.noaa.gov, outside the allowlist (F9; flagged by the verifier).
- This is a process breach that should be stated in the final report.

48-hour forecast path.summary: The 48h forecast cannot be audited event by event. Per-forecast rows, the NWS inputs and the page-load timing are all gone. Only three cumulative counter snapshots survive. Differencing them gives a flood-window model MAPE (mean absolute % error) of 5.2/7.1/8.5/23.0% at +6/12/24/48h, against persistence of 15.5/26.0/54.6%. Persistence at +48h is not derivable. In the hourly-issue simulation, for issues before 10-11T12 the mean client/server travel is 13.4/10.6 h at +6h and 13.4/4.3 h at +48h. The LF value scored differs from the LF at the client-built time by 12.1-22.2% mean (max 40.2%). For issues after 10-11T12 the gap is 1-3% mean. The simulation uses LF at issue as a proxy for the GF estimate, which on a rise is higher, so the true mismatch is larger. This is a scoring-clock effect, not forecast error. findings.title: Additive bias term is one fixed cfs value and its reference point can be a future NWS value
findings.what_happened: lfBiasOffset = observed LF minus interp(NWS LF, 0), added unchanged to every horizon. LF rose from 1,330 (10-09) to 24,300 cfs, about 18x. A proxy (observed LF minus LF k hours earlier, not NWS data) gives gaps of 3,800 cfs at 6 h and 9,600 at 12 h at 10-14T14, and -2,000/-4,800 on 10-15T12. A constant offset sized for the rise is therefore wrong for the recession, and wrong in sign. In addition, the NWS forecast array starts in the future (first point +2.7 h in the 2026-11-09 sample). With no point at or before 0, interpolateForecast(.,0) returns that first future point. On a rise that biases the offset downward. Maximum observed rises: 1,500 cfs/h, 4,100 per 3 h, 7,200 per 6 h. The actual NWS inputs are not recoverable, so the size of the error cannot be measured.

hydrology and travel time (gro.aspect: hydrology and travel time (ground truth vs app routing assumptions)
hydrology and travel time (gro.summary: Observed PoR->LF peak-to-peak was 14.1 h (PoR 26,300 at 10-14T00:40Z, LF 24,300 at 10-14T14:45Z, 92.4%). The Searcy-based travel model fits the falling limb above ~12,000 cfs (within ~1.5 h) and the high-flow front roughly, but the estimator's travel time was 2x too long on the early rise (25-57 h vs ~13 h observed) because the multiplier comes from a stale low historic PoR. The early LF rise (to ~11,500) was mostly explained by the four gauged tributaries, not ungauged runoff; only the first ~4 h is unexplained. Fixed fallback tributary ratios (11.6% of LF) were wrong by 10x at onset and 2x at peak but were never used (no tributary gaps). Data quality in the USGS record was good; LF stage rating in code is accurate. All figures are from one event, with lag-fit/fidelity caveats; the replay rows I cite are from the chosen lag setting and were not re-verified by me (rising-limb raw is unverified per replay notes), but the observed-hydrology numbers do not depend on the replay.

findings.title: Estimator travel time on the early rise was ~2x the observed PoR->LF lag
findings.what_happened: Between 10-13T00Z and 10-13T15Z the estimator's PoR->GF plus GF->LF travel was 25-32 h (historic PoR 2,900-3,000 cfs from 19-24 h earlier set the multiplier), while the observed lag for PoR flow to reach LF (LF net of gauged tribs) was 11-14 h. From 10-11T18Z to 10-12T18Z the estimator used 49-57 h against observed ~13 h on the main wave (the main wave had not started yet, so that window is not directly comparable, but the model was never going to see it coming). Once PoR passed ~16,000 (10-13T17Z on) the estimator total (10-13 h) was within 1-4 h of observed (13-14 h). The travel multiplier uses getFlowMultiplier(historicPoR.cfs), and on a rising river the lookup flow is low, so travel time is long, which in turn pulls an older, lower PoR value.
findings.evidence: q3_travel.txt section E and B; q6_display_vs_est.txt (e.g. 10-13T12Z estimator 32.3 h, hist PoR 3000 cfs at 24.3 h ago, PoR now 12,200; observed LF-net lag 13.3 h). Replay cols travel_por_gf_h, travel_gf_lf_h, historic_por_cfs (out/replay/replay_hourly.csv, chosen lag; fidelity on rising limb is timing-only, not raw-verified).
findings.recommendation: Do not derive the travel multiplier from the lagged historic PoR flow when the river is rising fast. Use max(current PoR, historic PoR) or the PoR flow at the front for the multiplier, then re-run the replay to see if rising-limb error drops. Treat as a hypothesis to test, since this is one event.

findings.title: The 'wave celerity' reduction (up to 30%) is contradicted on the rising limb of this event
findings.what_happened: Observed rising-limb crossing lags PoR->LF were 12.75 h (20,000), 13.5 h (22,000), 14.9 h (24,000) on raw LF, and 14-15 h net of tribs. Searcy at those flows without reduction gives 11.3, 10.7 and 10.2 h; with the 30% cap, ~7.9, 7.5 and 7.1 h. The reduction pushes the model further from observed. The falling limb matched the unreduced Searcy: 20,000 cfs observed 11.5 h vs 11.3 h model; 16,000 cfs 13.6 h vs 12.9 h; 12,000 cfs 16.8 h vs 15.4 h. Peak-to-peak 14.1 h vs model 9.6 h at 26,300 cfs (6.7 h with reduction).

findings.what_happened: calcTravelTimes shows baseHrs x Searcy multiplier at the current LF flow (PoR baseHrs 26). Because LF was inflated by tributary runoff (11,400 vs PoR 4,440 at 10-13T00Z), the display showed 16 h while the estimator was using 27.9-57.5 h. At 10-12T18Z display 16.6 h vs estimator 57.5 h. findings.evidence: q6_display_vs_est.txt / display_vs_estimator.csv; src/data/fetch.js calcTravelTimes lines 139-155.
findings.recommendation: Make the display and estimator share one travel-time definition, or label the display as flow-at-LF based. Note the display is closer to observed here, which argues for fixing H1 rather than the display.

findings.title: Early LF rise was mostly explained by gauged tributaries; unexplained local runoff is small and brief
findings.what_happened: LF first rose 100 cfs above baseline at 10-11T11:25Z, PoR at 07:55Z, Broad Run 11:30Z, Monocacy 13:25Z, Goose 13:40Z, Seneca 15:10Z. The LF hump (11,500 at 10-12T21Z to 10-13T00Z, held >11,000 until ~10-13T15Z) occurred while PoR was ~3,000: tributary sum peaked at 10,423 (10-12T15Z; Monocacy 6,660 at 10-12T17:30Z, Goose 2,660 at 09:30Z, Broad Run 2,150 at 14:55Z, Seneca 1,330 at 10-11T23Z). A lagged balance (PoR lagged 31 h, tribs lagged 6 h) on 10-11T12Z to 10-13T06Z gives RMSE 1,046 cfs, mean residual +52, range -1,280 to +2,262. The positive residual is concentrated 10-11T15Z to 21Z (+756, +2,110, +1,566 cfs, i.e. ~50% of LF at 10-11T18Z): LF began rising before any gauged trib could arrive (nearest, Seneca, baseHrs 5 h), so about 1,000 cfs of the first 4 h is ungauged local runoff. The replay note that the onset error is 'dominated by local runoff' should be softened: in the gauged data, the 10-11T21Z to 10-13T00Z LF level is explained by the four gauged tribs plus PoR to within ~1-1.5k cfs.
findings.evidence: q4_onset_mass.txt (onset thresholds, lagged residual table). The lag grid search was run on the same window it describes, so tp=31/tt=6 is in-sample.
findings.recommendation: Treat tributary timing, not ungauged runoff, as the main onset issue: the estimator adds tribs at their current value with no lag (see H6). Keep an ungauged-runoff allowance for the first ~4 h only.

findings.title: Tributaries are added at concurrent values although they peaked 5-14 h before they reached LF
findings.what_happened: Concurrent tributary sum plus PoR overshoots LF in the onset: at 10-11T18Z tribs 5,380 + PoR 2,230 = 7,610 against LF 4,050 (88% over); at 10-12T12Z 10,167 + 2,980 = 13,150 vs LF 8,340 (58% over). With the tributaries lagged ~6 h, the balance stays within about +/-2k. Gauged tributary flow is added without a travel-time shift in makeGFPrediction (porEstimateCFS = historicPoR.cfs + monocacyFlow + gooseFlow + ...).
findings.evidence: q4_onset_mass.txt decomposition and best-fit tables; scheduled-update.js lines 803-812.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate a per-tributary lag (about baseHrs x multiplier, 5-14 h) using the replay, and compare onset error. One event only; do not generalize the 6 h value.

findings.title: Fixed tributary fallback ratios (sum 11.6% of LF) are far from what the tributaries did in the flood
findings.what_happened: Measured gauged-tributary / LF ratio was 0.14 at baseline, 0.91 at 10-11T15Z, 1.16 at 10-11T21Z, 0.71 at 10-12T21Z, 0.18 at 10-13T18Z, 0.055 at LF peak, 0.077-0.12 on recession. The fallback therefore under-adds by about 10x at onset (e.g. 615 vs 6,150 cfs) and over-adds by 2x at the LF peak (2,826 vs 1,345). Per-tributary measured/fallback: Monocacy 0.4-9.5, Broad Run 1.1-65. This only matters when a tributary gauge is missing; in this record there were no gaps (cron may still have seen a stale value, see H9).
findings.evidence: q4_onset_mass.txt last ratio table; TRIB_FALLBACK in code/netlify/functions/shared/model.js lines 774-779.
findings.recommendation: Low priority. If a tributary is missing during a surge the fallback would be badly wrong; consider failing to a stale last-known value or flagging the estimate as low-confidence instead. No change needed from this event.

findings.title: Mass balance: LF volume is 2-5% below PoR plus gauged tributaries; peak attenuation ~8-13%
findings.what_happened: 10-11T00Z to 10-19T12Z volume: LF 225.5 Mm3 vs PoR+tribs 235.9 (no lag) or 230.9 (12 h lag), so LF is 2.4-4.6% lower, and excess over the 10-11T06Z baseline is 195.3 vs 200.7 Mm3 (-2.8%). No net ungauged contribution is visible in volume. At the crest, LF 24,300 vs PoR peak 26,300 (92.4%); LF minus concurrent tribs peaked at 22,991 (87.4% of PoR peak) at 10-14T16:20Z. With PoR lagged 8-16 h plus measured tribs, LF was 7.7-10.9% lower than the sum over 10-14T06Z to 10-15T12Z (mean -1,664 to -2,390 cfs); with the fallback ratios the shortfall is 12.9-16.1%. Consistent with storage attenuation, but provisional rating bias at PoR or LF is equally plausible and cannot be separated here.
findings.evidence: q4_onset_mass.txt (volume and mass-balance sections); q3_travel.txt section A.
findings.recommendation: none. The app's attenuation is implicit in the learned corrections; note that using the 11.6% fallback at peak would add ~1,500 cfs of error in the wrong direction (H7).

findings.title: USGS record is gap-free and well-formed, but it hides what the cron actually saw
findings.what_happened: Every series has a perfect cadence in the file: PoR, LF, Broad Run, Seneca every 5 min (4,897 points each, 10-04T23Z to 10-21T23Z); Monocacy, Goose, Edwards Ferry every 15 min (1,633). Zero gaps, zero non-positive values, all 'P' except Monocacy 'A' for 10-04T23Z to 10-07T14:30Z (before the event). Longest flat runs in the event window are quantization or rounding, not dead gauges: PoR 1,200 for 2.25 h on 10-11 (pre-rise), LF 11,000 for 2.1 h at the hump bottom (10-13T08:40Z), Seneca 143 for 3 h and 74 for 2.6 h, Goose in recession up to 5.25 h at constant 227-259 cfs (Goose reports in coarse steps at low flow). findings.recommendation: none for the record itself. Keep the replay's per-gauge lag fit as the only evidence of cron-time staleness.

findings.title: Edwards Ferry stage responds to Monocacy before the PoR wave and over-reads flow at the crest
findings.what_happened: EF stage rose 3.1 ft to 6.2 ft (10-10T12Z to 10-12T21Z) while PoR was only ~3,000 cfs, tracking Monocacy (peak 6,660 at 10-12T17:30Z). The EF power-law estimate was already 10,470-10,902 cfs at 10-12T16-20Z (PoR+Monocacy then ~8,000-9,000, and LF ~11,000). At the crest EF stage peaked 9.2 ft at 10-14T08:00Z (7.3 h after the PoR peak, 6.75 h before the LF peak) and the replay's EF estimate was 29,679 cfs at that tick, versus about 27,350 cfs for PoR peak plus Monocacy then (+8.5%) and 26,300 at the PoR peak. The EF weight was capped at 0.39-0.40 so the effect on the final estimate is bounded (ef_used true, discrepancy 3.9-17%). EF stage at a given PoR flow differed by 1.4-1.7 ft between rising and falling limbs (5,000 cfs: 6.22 vs 4.85 ft; 20,000: 7.13 vs 8.83 ft), which is largely timing (EF lags PoR by ~7 h plus Monocacy).

findings.recommendation: Keep EF weight capped. Record in the audit that EF is a 7-hour-ahead signal of LF crest and is also driven by Monocacy, so its 'agreement' with PoR+tribs is not independent confirmation. No change from one event.

findings.title: PoR hydrograph was two-phase; early PoR bump masked the main wave in any rise-rate logic
findings.what_happened: PoR rose 1,250 to 2,980 (10-11T06Z to 10-12T12Z), plateaued about 2,900-3,000 for ~10 h, then the main wave started ~10-12T20Z: 3,410 (21Z) -> 12,300 (10-13T12Z) -> 26,300 (10-14T00:40Z). Rise rates in the replay jumped from ~0.3-1.2 %/h to 17-18 %/h at 10-13T03-06Z. What the user was shown and wh.aspect: What the user was shown and whether it was honest (CI band, confidence label, 120% ceiling, advisory banners, stage, How It Works text)
What the user was shown and wh.summary: The displays were mostly dishonest in the two phases that mattered most. In the onset the app under-read badly and nothing flagged it. In the recession the 90% band missed every validation for about 2.5 days and no banner fired. The 120%-of-LF ceiling cut both ways: it tamed a ~+25% raw overshoot on the rise and, if the unverified replay raw is right, turned a roughly unbiased raw into a ~-38% under-read in the onset. Stage conversion and the rating curve held up well. Everything is one event, server-side replay only (lag setting por55/lf10/mono5/goose5/broadrun50/seneca20/ef45 + LF overrides, uniform-lag files checked), and no browser estimate was replayed. Rising-limb raw values are unverified: 1 of 24 onset ticks and 6 of 54 rise ticks carry any fidelity evidence. Pre-10-15T16 corrected values are a bracket, not what was displayed. Scripts and outputs are in /private/tmp/claude-503/-Users-sebjilke/252f7c3c-5965-4854-a165-14468fc066da/scratchpad/pulse-audit/out/display/.

findings.title: 90% band covered far less than 90% and missed all 14 consecutive recession validations
findings.what_happened: On the 41 logged validations (displayed predictedCFS, logged bin/state, app-truth LF) the band held the actual 20/41 (49%). By phase of prediction creation: pre-event 6/6, onset 0/1, rise 4/6, peak 3/6, recession 7/22 (32%). The 14 validations from 10-16T00 to 10-18T20 all fell outside the band (errors -4.9% to -13.8%). Reason: 6000-12000/falling q05/q95 = -451/+359 cfs, about +/-4-5% at 8-10k cfs, against a realised bias of -6 to -14%. The band was calibrated on the 2011-2026 prequential backtest and the learned bin SD is tiny (174-202 cfs), so it was narrow and wrong together. On the 313-tick replay with physical truth (approx1015 bracket) coverage was 132/313 (42%): pre 96%, onset 8%, rise 65%, peak 56%, recession 11%. With exact bins, 3/97 (3%) from 10-15T16 to 10-19T16. The CI is shown in the Inputs panel as a '90% CI' row, not in the headline.
findings.evidence: out/display/ci_coverage.py -> ci_coverage.txt, ci_coverage_logged41.csv; EMPIRICAL_CI_90 at code/src/model/constants.js:95, applied at code/src/estimation/great-falls.js:87-108 as [est - q95, est - q05]; UI row at code/src/ui/great-falls-ui.js:251
findings.recommendation: Treat the band as miscalibrated for out-of-regime states. Add a coverage monitor on live validations (rolling hit rate for the last N pairs, not only a backtest). Widen or hide the band when the last k validations all miss on the same side. Do not let learned bin SD alone set display width. One event: this is a signal, not a calibrated miss rate.

findings.title: Confidence label carried almost no information about realised error
findings.what_happened: Reconstructed label (INFERRED: client logic, EF trend from USGS EF stage at 45 min lag, server flow state, logged banner episodes). Median |error| by label over all 313 ticks: HIGH 9.4% (n=47), MEDIUM 9.0% (n=191), LOW 9.0% (n=75). Share of ticks over 25% error: HIGH 4%, MEDIUM 5%, LOW 12%. 6 of the 52 ticks with error >15% and 2 of the 20 with error >25% were labelled HIGH. Onset ticks (all had >15% error) were labelled low/medium/high at 10/12/2. The label flickered low/medium/high hour to hour through the rise because it depends on EF-trend agreement with a flow state that flickers. The legend says Medium = 'could shift 10-20%'; onset-medium ticks had median error 36%. Before the event the EF banner pushed the label to LOW on 50 of 72 ticks (median error 7%), which devalues LOW.

findings.recommendation: Derive the label from realised recent error (last validated errors, ceiling-bound flag, advisory state), not from tributary availability and EF trend agreement. Make LOW mean something by not downgrading for 8 days of low-flow EF noise. Confirm in the browser: the client trend and rise rate may differ from this reconstruction.

findings.title: 120% ceiling: displayed number was literally 1.2 x LF for most of onset and rise; it helped on the rise and hurt at onset; it is never shown to the user
findings.what_happened: Stored and validated predictedCFS is the CLIPPED value (rawFinalCFS is the unclipped learning target, scheduled-update.js:897-899, 1028-1031). Replay raw-ceiling-bound ticks: pre 15/72 (mean excess 79 cfs), onset 11/24 (mean 2,813, max 4,604 cfs), rise 46/54 (mean 3,004, max 7,483), peak 5/18 (mean 4,250, max 6,536), recession 0/145. On the approx-corrected display, 10 onset, 27 rise and 4 peak ticks were bound, and the shown value equals ceiling_limit_cfs (1.2 x LF reading up to 70 min stale) on every one of them. On rise and peak the clip removed a ~+25% raw overshoot: MAPE 12.2% clipped vs 25.4% unclipped on rise-bound ticks, bias +0.9% vs +25.2%; peak 4.3% vs 23.4%. At onset the clip hurt: clipped bias -38.1% (MAPE 38.1%) vs unclipped bias -2.0% (MAPE 34.5%), unclipped closer on 7 of 11 bound ticks. The same ordering holds at L0, L60 and L75 (onset clipped bias -40/-44/-45%, unclipped -1/-8/-11%). The UI never surfaces ceilingApplied (returned at great-falls.js:595, no consumer in src/ui). On bound ticks the shown label was medium on all 10 onset ticks and high/medium/low (9/9/9) on rise. Caveat: the onset 'unclipped is nearly unbiased' result rests on replayed raw values that are UNVERIFIABLE (no logged raw between 10-11T12 and 10-14T06); the bound/LF-view part is verified (8/8 ceiling-implied LF values reproduced).
findings.evidence: out/display/ceiling.py -> ceiling.txt (L0/L60/L75 sections included); code/netlify/functions/shared/model.js:713-722 (applyGFCorrection); index.html docs text
findings.recommendation: Show 'capped at 120% of Little Falls' state to the user when the ceiling binds, and downgrade confidence while it does. Do not describe a bound number as a model estimate. Study an upstream-aware cap (use the PoR/tributary evidence when LF is the thing that is lagging) before the next event. Do not remove the cap on the evidence of one event, since it protected the rise.

findings.title: Advisory banners: up for the wrong reasons at onset, down for the whole recession bias, and silent through the flood proper
findings.what_happened: Logged episodes (Supabase SELECT confirmed): EF divergence 10-03T07 to 10-11T14 (five rows, 129+24+23+2+5 cycles), nothing after. LF-residual 10-11T12 to 10-12T00 (1 pair, -16.1%) and 10-12T02 to 10-13T03 (2 pairs, worst -72.9%), nothing after. Banner-up ticks 117/313. Ticks with error >15% and no banner of either kind: 12 of 52 (approx series); 13/61 with the raw-displayed series. Ticks with error >25% and no banner: 2 of 20. But the banner was up at onset largely by coincidence: the EF banner was a left-over low-flow episode that ended at 10-11T14, and the LF-residual latched on a -16.1% low-flow pair at 10-11T12. The first flood-driven residual pair (-72.9%) latched only at 10-12T02. That is about 26 h after the first >25% error tick (10-11T03), and the 10-11T12 prediction that made it was still scored 14 h later. There was a 2 h gap (10-12T00, T01) with the banner down at 15-19% error. The residual banner dropped at 10-13T03 (12 h staleness after the 10-12T15 pair; the next pair arrived 10-13T07 at +16.8%, which cleared the latch). Large-error runs with no banner: 10-13T12..16 (5 ticks, mean -19%, bracket-only, UNVERIFIABLE) and 10-17T13. False alarms: pre-event banner-up ticks with error <=15% = 63 of 70 (EF banner on 70 of 72 ticks over 3 days of ordinary low-flow noise). EF banner could not fire in the flood: detector fell inactive at 10-11T16 (dbar 0.92 -> 0.36) because the PoR-based estimate was inflated by tributaries while EF was skipped for >50% discrepancy at 10-11T18 to 10-12T02.

findings.recommendation: Judge banners against validated-error timing, not tick timing: they are structurally 13 h late at onset because the single pending slot and 13 h travel time delay the first pair. Add a non-validation trigger (LF rising fast while the estimate lags, or ceiling bound) so the banner can fire before a pair validates. Replace the 8-day EF banner with a rule that does not fire on steady low-flow noise.

findings.title: Residual banner stayed down through the -6 to -14% recession run because of its thresholds and latch design
findings.what_happened: Rule: latch on at errorPercentCorrected <= -15, clear at > -7.5, hold in between, stale after 12 h. After the +16.8% pair at 10-13T07 the latch was cleared. The recession pairs ran -4.1% (10-15T06) to -13.8% (10-17T13). The worst was 1.2 points short of -15, so it could never re-latch. From 10-16T00 to 10-18T20 there were 14 consecutive same-sign errors of -4.9% to -13.8%, with a mean around -10%. Hard-flagged pairs do feed the banner (pairs.push includes hardFlagged), so censoring is not the cause. Design cause: a magnitude threshold with no persistence term. Realised cost: roughly 100 hourly ticks of -9% median under-read with 'MEDIUM/HIGH' labels and no banner (recession approx MAPE 8.7%, bias -8.6%; exact-bins 9.3%/-9.1%).
findings.evidence: out/display/banners.py (last section lists each logged validation against the -15/-7.5 thresholds); code/netlify/functions/shared/model.js:271-312 (LF_RESIDUAL); scheduled-update.js:1665
findings.recommendation: Add a persistence rule (e.g. k consecutive same-sign errors beyond 5%) so a steady -9% to -14% run trips the advisory. This is a calibrated trade-off against false alarms and needs its own gate. This finding describes one event.

findings.title: Stage: rating relation is accurate; stage errors are small and understate flow errors; the logged stage columns are raw-basis
findings.what_happened: Against 3,744 paired LF readings (10-08 to 10-21), observed stage minus estimateLFStage(observed cfs): overall mean +0.006 ft, MAE 0.021 ft, max |0.06| ft, and no systematic rise/fall hysteresis (rise vs fall residual differences <=0.02 ft in every band). Peak: 24,300 cfs, 5.26 ft observed vs 5.20 ft rating. estimateLFFlowFromStage is an exact inverse (max round-trip difference 0.000 cfs over 100-60,000). The range seen (to 24.3k cfs) never reached the 28k+ segments, so those are untested here. Logged hard-flag stage errors: mean -0.031 ft, MAE 0.14 ft, extremes -0.72 ft (10-11T12 row, 2.79 vs 3.51) and +0.54/+0.29 ft at 10-14T06/T09. Those two overshoots are in the snapshot's predictedStage, which equals the RAW stage (stage(27,535)=5.46), so the displayed clipped stage (20,880 cfs -> 4.93 ft vs 4.92 ft actual) was right. Replay stage MAE: onset 0.40-0.46 ft, rise 0.15-0.26, peak 0.05-0.16, recession 0.06-0.10. Because the rating is shallow, a -13% flow miss shows as only about -0.1 ft, so the 'Stage Error ~0.08 ft' headline looks much better than the flow error.
