Rating-curve behaviour above 28,000 cfs; this event peaked at 24,300 cfs / 5.26 ft

correction, learning and caden.summary: One event, 41 scored validations, all UTC, error = estimate - actual. Learning machinery was deterministic and reproducible. The correction layer was inert on the rise, because the 120%-of-LF ceiling set every scored display value. It was harmful in the recession, because the Check-5 outlier gate froze a bin at the wrong sign. The single pending slot left the onset essentially unscored: 1 of 26 hourly predictions, with the first validation arriving 14 h after the surge began. Flow-state labels follow Point of Rocks, so they disagreed with the Little Falls direction on 37% of hourly ticks. Rising-limb raw values are replay-only and unverified. Counterfactuals are in-sample upper bounds. Scripts and outputs are in the learning/ folder.

findings.title: Check-5 outlier gate froze a wrong-sign bin through the recession
findings.what_happened: 12 consecutive hard-flagged validations (validated 10-16T00 to 10-18T07; 2 in 12000-25000 falling, 10 in 6000-12000 falling) were all rejected by STATISTICAL_OUTLIER alone (z 3.1 to 5.7). The 6000-12000/falling bin was learned in an earlier regime (n=17, cumulative mean +231, SD 174 cfs, EMA +401), so any under-read beyond -289 cfs (about 4% at 7,000 cfs) counted as an outlier. The recession under-read the river by 3 to 9% (raw MAPE 5.56%). The frozen +401 correction was subtracted anyway, which made things worse: corrected MAPE 9.22%, and the correction moved the estimate closer to truth in 0 of 12 rows. The bin was still n=17, EMA +401 in the 11-10 snapshot. Counterfactual with all 12 rows allowed into learning, in order, through the real updateCorrectionBin and C45 interpolation: MAPE 3.06%. With the soft-flag path (clamped to +-2 sigma): 3.48%. The counterfactual is in-sample, from autocorrelated rows of one recession, so it is an upper bound. The smallest rejected raw error was -1.9% (10-15T09, -366 cfs, z=3.7), so a normal-size error was gated out.
findings.evidence: out/learning/s5_rejection_cost.cjs -> s5_rejection_cost.txt (recomputed z matches logged z on every row); s1_validation_table.txt (recession hard-flag rows: raw bias -5.6%, corrected -9.2%, 0/12 helped; 6000-12000 steady clean: raw -2.8%, corrected -8.0%, 0/4); data/snapshot-2026-11-10-gf.json (6000-12000 falling n=17, ema 401). Check 5 at code/netlify/functions/scheduled-update.js lines 1170-1186.
findings.recommendation: Do not hard-reject on a z-score against a cumulative SD from a different regime. Options: make Check 5 a soft flag (learn clamped), require an absolute error floor (for example >15%) before hard-flagging, or use a recent-window SD. Separately, stop applying a correction from a bin whose recent rejected errors have the opposite sign. Apply the same fix to the frozen +401 bin that is still in force.

findings.title: On the rise the ceiling set every scored display value; the learned correction never showed
findings.what_happened: All 8 scored predictions created 10-12T02 to 10-14T09 were displayed at 1.2 x a stale LF reading (8 of 8 logged ceiling-implied values matched exactly). In the replay, the raw estimate exceeded the ceiling on 62 of 72 hourly ticks (10-11T13 to 10-14T12), by a mean 3,070 cfs and a max 7,483. Logged corrected error on those 8 rows was MAPE about 7.9% (-21.6, +1.6, +16.8, -1.7, +15.0, -0.7, +3.9, +1.8). Replay raw on the 6 clean rising rows was +31.5% MAPE (unverified). So the ceiling guard did the work, but at 1.2 x a reading up to 70 min old on a river rising up to 1,400 cfs/h, which gave -21.6% on 10-12T15. Meanwhile learning used the unclipped raw error. The 12000-25000/rising bin therefore learned about +3,762 from regime-specific over-reads that were never displayed, and it stays in force for the next rise.
findings.evidence: s6_edges_and_thin.txt (ceiling counts); s1_validation_table.txt (rising-limb ceiling-bound rows: raw 31.5% vs corrected 9.6%, 6/6 closer); out/replay/fidelity_table.csv (8/8 ceiling-implied LF match). Rising-limb raw is replay-only.
findings.recommendation: Report ceiling-bound validations separately in accuracy, and do not let ceiling-masked rows train a correction that will be applied unmasked later. Consider a rise-aware ceiling that uses the LF rate of change instead of a fixed 1.2 x stale reading.

findings.title: Single pending slot left the onset nearly unscored and delayed learning and the advisory
findings.what_happened: Of 26 hourly predictions from 10-11T13 to 10-12T14, one was stored and scored. Validation gaps on the rise were 14, 13, 16, 7, 9, 3, 4 and 3 h, while LF rose +4,550, +3,260, +1,690, +300, +2,400, +700, +3,100 and +3,800 cfs in those gaps. Over 10-11T13 to 10-14T06 there were 66 hourly predictions and 7 validations, so a per-tick design would have produced about 9.4 times as many. LF passed 3,000 cfs at 10-11T15:45. The first validation of the flood (10-12T02, -72.9%) was hard-flagged and not learned. The first flood observation to enter learning was 10-12T15, 23 h after onset. The LF-residual advisory only latched at 10-12T02. In the replay, hourly validation would have produced a corrected error of -29% by due 10-11T14:12, so the advisory could have latched about 12 h earlier. The effective detection latency equals the travel time (13-16 h) because validations only arrive one travel time after the prediction.
findings.evidence: s4_cadence.txt; s7_advisory_latency.txt; out/replay/replay_hourly.csv chain_stored. Counterfactual uses approx1015 bins and physical truth (a bracket); raw errors on the rise are replay-only.
findings.recommendation: Allow multiple pending predictions (or a short-horizon check against current LF) so the advisory and the learner react within hours, not a full travel time. A rate-of-change trigger on LF alone would have fired at the onset.

findings.title: Flow-state label follows Point of Rocks trend, not the Little Falls state at validation
findings.what_happened: Of 313 hourly ticks, 63% of labels matched the LF direction over the validation horizon (74% of the 47 stored). By phase: onset 62%, rise 61%, peak 50%, recession 68%. At the crest the label said 'steady' at 10-14T05 and T06 (LF +24% and +20% to due) and then 'falling' from 10-14T07 to T12 while LF still rose +18, +13, +17, +8, +4 and +2% to due. The bin key (rising, steady or falling) was therefore wrong for the target gauge in most of the crest window. Labels also flicker on a flat river: in the replay at 10-12T19 to T20 the label flipped falling to steady and the unclipped corrected value moved -3,677 cfs for a -1,115 cfs raw change. At 10-18T15 to T16 (exact bins) steady and rising alternated with swings of +910 and -910 cfs.
findings.evidence: s3_state_labels.py -> s3_state_labels.csv/.txt; s6_edges_and_thin.txt. Pre-10-15T16 corrections are approx1015 (bracket), the 10-18 flicker uses exactbins.
findings.recommendation: Add hysteresis (a minimum dwell time) to flow-state and consider keying the correction on the expected LF direction over the travel time rather than the PoR trend. At minimum, do not let PoR noise at flat flow switch bins.

findings.title: Edge smoothing works at 3k/6k/12k on the falling limb but leaves a hard step at 25k and a non-monotone ramp on the rising state
findings.what_happened: Went well: the falling-limb ramp across 12,000 was smooth (observed in-force corrections 82, 188, 290, 378, 401 as raw fell 13,503 to 10,313), which avoids a 320 cfs step. Not well: (a) the 25,000 edge is an unsmoothed step: displayed value jumps -1,071 cfs for 2 cfs of raw on the falling state (-1,220 with the 10-19 bins), +491 rising, +458 steady. (b) In the rising state the 12k band (raw 10,714 to 13,440, +2,726) moves the correction from -998 to +3,760, so the displayed value falls 2,033 cfs (11,712 to 9,680) while raw rises. Only the ceiling hid this during the flood; in replay raw rose while the unclipped corrected value fell in 2 hourly pairs. (c) The 6k band rising shows +2,962 displayed for +1,363 raw. The largest hourly applied-correction jump was 3.4k at 10-11T17 (replay, approx bins).
findings.evidence: s2_bin_jumps.cjs -> s2_bin_jumps.txt (real getGFCorrectionInterpolated); s6_edges_and_thin.txt (21 of 312 hourly pairs with a >=500 cfs correction change). Bins are the 10-15T16 snapshot and the 10-19T16 bins.
findings.recommendation: Smooth the 25,000 and 50,000 edges or clamp |d correction / d raw| to below 1 so the displayed value stays monotone in raw. Add a monotonicity test over all three states.

findings.title: Thin and extreme bins carried large corrections; one is inconsistent with the replay and is still in force
findings.what_happened: 12000-25000/steady is n=1 with EMA 9,743 (still n=1 on 11-10). The blend (weight 1/5 on the one observation) applied +2,792 cfs on every steady tick in that bin. 6000-12000/rising is n=4 with EMA -1,350, blended to -1,000, so +1,000 cfs was added on the rising limb. In the 10-15 snapshot, 42 hourly ticks fell in these thin bins, 5 of them scored. The one rising-limb bin with a checkable constraint disagrees with the replay: the bin implies raw = 11,000 + 9,743 = 20,743 for the 10-12T15 to 10-13T07 prediction, but the replay raw is 16,401 (-4,342 cfs, -20.9%), identical across lags L0 to L75. So either that bin contains another observation, or the replay under-reads raw at that tick, which weakens trust in replayed rising-limb raw values. 12000-25000/rising (n=7, +3,762) is also a flood-learned correction.
findings.evidence: s2_bin_jumps.txt (thin-bin blends); s6_edges_and_thin.txt (n=1 check, lag files); data/captured_context_2026-10.json bin_snapshots; data/snapshot-2026-11-10-gf.json.
findings.recommendation: Raise the minimum count for any bin correction above a few hundred cfs (or cap the correction at a fraction of flow), and reset or decay n<5 bins at the end of an event. Reconcile the 20,743 vs 16,401 raw before relying on replayed rising-limb raw.

findings.title: Low-flow correction helped on average pre-event but one correction produced the only pre-flood miss and latched the advisory
findings.what_happened: Pre-event (6 validations to 10-11T12) correction cut MAPE from 13.0% (raw, bias +13.0%) to 5.9%, closer in 5 of 6. In-force corrections of 155 to 329 cfs on a roughly 1,500 cfs river (10 to 22% of flow) fit a model that over-read base flow. The exception was 10-11T12: raw 1,525 was 0.3% off 1,520, but the in-force 0-3000/falling correction (249 cfs) gave 1,276, a -16.1% error. That error latched the LF-residual advisory (onset threshold -15%) from 10-11T12 to 10-12T00 for the wrong reason. The advisory lapsed 2 h before the real surge latched it at 10-12T02. Four earlier low-flow rows were hard-flagged by the v37.20 ice gate (fixed in v37.21).
findings.evidence: s1_validation_table.txt (pre-event line and 10-11T12 row); out/replay/advisory_compare.txt; data/captured_context_2026-10.json.
findings.recommendation: None for the correction itself. Treat a state label of 'falling' at a flat 1,500 cfs as low-confidence for bin selection (see L4).

findings.title: Hard-flag censoring removed most of the recession from the headline, but the headline barely moves
findings.what_happened: Of the 24 validations from 10-14T09 to 10-18T07, 16 were hard-flagged (all 16 by Check 5; EF_DISCREPANCY is a soft flag) and 8 were clean. Counting all 17 flood hard-flagged rows (validated 10-12T02 to 10-18T07, mean absolute corrected error 11.5%) would move avgErrorPercent from 7.3755 to 7.549 (+0.17 pp). Counting only the 12 consecutive recession rows gives 7.430. The 10-12T02 row (-72.9%, the largest miss of the event) is excluded too. So the headline is insensitive to censoring, but it hides the 12 under-read rows and the largest miss. Between 10-15T16 and 10-19T16 only 5 rows were added to the denominator (387 to 392 valid).
findings.evidence: s5_rejection_cost.txt (headline block); data/captured_context_2026-10.json metadata_snapshots; data/snapshot-2026-11-10-validation-failures.json.
findings.recommendation: Publish accuracy with and without hard-flagged rows, and count statistical-outlier rows separately from data-corruption flags.

findings.title: Learning arithmetic and C45 interpolation are reproducible; the recession falling bin converged correctly while it was allowed to learn
findings.what_happened: From 10-15T16 the exact-bins replay reproduces the logged corrected values on 17 of 17 rows (max 0.57%) and the in-force corrections within 4 cfs. 12000-25000/falling went from (n=23, +230) to (n=24, +81) as expected. Clean-row learning on the falling limb from 10-14T21 to 10-15T20 (8 rows) had MAPE 2.1% raw vs 2.5% corrected, so it was neutral there. The corrected estimate beat raw on the crest-window rows (10-14T09 to T18 validated, MAPE 5.3% vs 18.9% raw), though that mostly reflects the ceiling.
findings.evidence: out/replay/fidelity_table.csv; s1_validation_table.txt (recession 10-14T21 to 10-15T20 line); s2_bin_jumps.txt.
findings.recommendation: none

findings.title: LF-residual advisory lapsed by design during gaps and stayed silent through a persistent recession under-read
findings.what_happened: The advisory expires 12 h after the last validated pair. The 16 h gap between validations 10-12T15 and 10-13T07 let it lapse near 10-13T03 while LF was still rising toward 24,300 cfs. The replay shows the same behaviour with a seconds-level race at the 12 h edge (it ends 10-13T04 in the replay vs 10-13T03 logged). During the recession all 12 corrected errors were -3.4% to -13.8%, none at or beyond the -15% latch, so the advisory never fired despite a consistent 9% under-read.
findings.evidence: code/netlify/functions/shared/model.js lines 262-300 (onPct -15, offPct -7.5, stale 12 h); out/replay/advisory_compare.txt; s1_validation_table.txt.
findings.recommendation: Consider a lower latch threshold or a persistent-bias rule (for example 5 consecutive same-sign errors beyond 5%), and extend the staleness window or trigger on LF rate of change.

not_observable: Correction bins before the flood (pre 10-15T16 values are the approx bracket; the 10-12 to 10-15 in-force corrections are known only on rows where raw was logged and the ceiling did not bind).

Bin state (count, sumError, sumErrorSq) at the moment each Check-5 decision was made; z values are reproduced only for the 12 recession rows against the 11-10 frozen bin, and those flag decisions are taken as logged.
Raw estimates on the rising limb 10-11T12 to 10-14T06 (replay-only; no logged raw), including whether the 20,743 vs 16,401 raw mismatch on 10-12T15 is a replay error or an unseen bin observation.
The two extra observations in 12000-25000/rising (n=7 vs 5 identifiable clean rows) and the pre-flood composition of 25000-50000 and 6000-12000/rising bins.

What a per-tick validation design would actually have learned or flagged (the counterfactuals in L1 and L3 are in-sample, assume physical truth and the approx bins, and ignore how Check 5 would interact with extra observations).
What paddlers saw in the browser estimate (client-side flow state, rise rate and localStorage history differ from the server cron), and per-tick stale-input delivery at gauges other than LF.
Great Falls flow itself: all errors are against Little Falls including ungauged inflow below Great Falls, so part of the onset error is unmodelable local runoff.

operations and data plumbing d.aspect: operations and data plumbing during the event
operations and data plumbing d.summary: The hourly cron ran every tick across the event window. No missed run is recorded from 10-07T21 to 10-19T16, and two independent log trails agree. The weak points are about what was logged, not what ran. No gauge has a freshness guard in the estimate. LF was 65-70 min stale on 3 of 39 logged ticks and nothing recorded it. The shadow leaderboard cannot speak to this event. A second, unknown writer created the rise_event rows, and the app does not read them. Much of the event's evidence is gone or was never stored: clean-row flags, input vectors, the original PoR values and pre-event bin states. One partial recovery: gf_correction_bin created_at plus the clean-row list bound how much of the 10-15 bins is flood learning, and it is less than the plan assumed for bins at or above 25,000 cfs. All times UTC. This is one event, so these are observations.

findings.title: Cron ran every hourly tick through the event; no miss recorded 10-07T21 to 10-19T16
findings.what_happened: gf_metadata.consecutiveRuns went 188 (10-15T16) to 285 (10-19T16) with missedRuns flat at 655. 188 implies the streak began 10-07T21, so the last miss was the 10-07T20 tick. The EF-divergence episode trails (one entry per cron run) show 0 gaps over 70 min from 10-07T21 to 10-11T13. Those 89 ticks are 85 trail ticks plus 4 one-tick deactivations. Before that the same trails show 26 missing hours in two earlier episodes. Every advisory episode starting 10-09T05 or later has cycles equal to elapsed hours, including lf_residual 10-11T12 to 10-12T00 (12/12) and 10-12T02 to 10-13T03 (25/25). 21 hard-flag rows were validated at minute 0, 14-26 s past the hour. 454 consecutive runs at 11-09T22 imply a restart at 10-22T01, so the single later miss (missedRuns 656) was the 10-22T00 tick, after the event.
findings.evidence: out/ops/cron_timing.py (.out); out/ops/episode_cycles.py (.out); DB SELECT on ef_divergence_episode and lf_residual_episode; data/captured_context_2026-10.json metadata_snapshots. NOTES.md section (a).
findings.recommendation: none. The one residue is a +-1 mismatch: the counter moved 97 over 96 h, probably snapshot timing, unresolved.

findings.title: Run-health and heartbeat cannot see a run that completed but produced no prediction; no per-tick trail after 10-11T14
findings.what_happened: updateRunHealth fires on every run that does not throw. makeGFPrediction returns null when LF or PoR q is missing, and the run is still counted healthy and pings healthchecks success. A run that throws before updateRunHealth counts as a miss on the next run, so that case is covered. Per-tick evidence after 10-11T14 exists only as counters and the two lf_residual episodes, because the EF advisory was inactive from then on. Continuity for roughly 194 flood ticks (10-11T14 to 10-19T16) therefore rests mostly on two counters.
findings.evidence: code/netlify/functions/scheduled-update.js lines 1743-1780 (computeRunHealth, updateRunHealth) and 2094-2210 (handler; null prediction path); NOTES.md (a).
findings.recommendation: Add a tiny per-run record (tick time, prediction produced yes/no, reason if null, per-gauge reading dateTimes) and ping /fail or a distinct signal when prediction is null.

findings.title: No staleness guard on any gauge used by the estimate; LF was 65-70 min stale on 3 of 39 logged ticks and this was not recorded
findings.what_happened: fetchUSGSData takes the last value of each series with no age check. Only the EF stage age (2 h) is checked, and only inside the divergence advisory. A tributary with q missing falls back to lf.q times a drainage ratio silently. The replay's fitted lags are LF 10 min, PoR 55, Broad Run 50, EF 45, Seneca 20, Monocacy and Goose 5. Only LF is directly observed: 36 of 39 logged LF actuals match a reading at most 10 min old, and 3 need 65-70 min (10-14T09, 10-14T21, 10-15T09). At 10-14T09 the cron had 20,100 cfs against 21,400 now on file. The 120%-of-LF ceiling uses this stale lf.q. It bound 46 of 54 rise ticks, 11 of 24 onset, 5 of 18 peak and 0 of 145 recession, with the same counts at every uniform lag from 0 to 75 min. Four one-tick EF-advisory deactivations (10-09T04, 10-10T05, 10-11T05, 10-11T08) are probably EF readings over 2 h old; this is inferred, not proven. Today's USGS file has no gap over 30 min and shows 0.3 min age at every tick, so it cannot show what the cron saw.
findings.evidence: out/ops/usgs_latency.py (.out); out/replay/lf_overrides.csv and best_lags.json; out/ops/ceiling_vs_lag.py (.out); scheduled-update.js lines 210-290 and 802-806; shared/model.js EF_DIVERGENCE.efMaxAgeMs.
findings.recommendation: Store the dateTime of each reading used on the pending row and in gf_history. Log a warning and mark the prediction when LF or PoR is older than about 45 min. Record tributary-fallback use as a flag. Reconsider anchoring the ceiling to a stale LF on the rising limb.

findings.title: rise_event: written by a second writer that is not in this codebase; nothing in the app reads it
findings.what_happened: The frozen export has zero references to rise_event in src/ or netlify/. v37.1 (2026-06-18) retired System-1 and deleted 9 rise_event rows, calling them a legacy artifact. Yet 9 new rows exist, created 2026-06-18T20:30 to 2026-07-10T00:45, one per upstream gauge, on a 15-minute grid (:00, :15, :30, :45). The app's cron is hourly. A metadata/system row {risesDetected: 2, lastRun 06-18T20:30:00.857Z} was written the same second as the first two. That row has never been updated since, which fits an insert-only writer. Two explanations fit: the writer stopped after 07-10, or it inserts and the unique key (observation_type, gauge_id) lets each gauge write once. The second would block October even for PoR 01638500, which already held a 07-06 row. The data cannot separate the two. The October flood, the season's largest, produced no rows. The code cannot depend on rise_event, so the app is unaffected.
findings.evidence: DB SELECT on observation_type in (rise_event, metadata, snapshot): 9 rows, 9 distinct gauge ids; grep over code/ (no hits outside analysis/system1-retirement-plan-2026-06-18.md and CHANGELOG.md); NOTES.md (c).
findings.recommendation: Locate and disable the orphan writer (an old deploy, another scheduler or another project), then delete the 9 rise_event rows and the metadata/system row. Do not read it into any analysis.

findings.title: Shadow leaderboard cannot say anything about this event, and its leader is largely an LF-persistence model
findings.what_happened: One cumulative row (reset 2026-05-28, last updated 11-09T15): 393 rounds, mean abs error kalman 7.96%, lfFeedback 10.12%, onlineRegression 11.06%, production on the RAW error 12.97%. The headline accuracy of 7.28% is the corrected model and is a different quantity. There is no snapshot around the event and only sums are stored, with no variance or CI. shadowModels sit on the pending row and are deleted at validation. Scoring skips hard-flagged rows, which removed 16 of 18 rows from 10-14T06 to 10-18T01. The event can contribute at most the 21 clean rows, 5.3% of 393. Kalman and onlineRegression ingest the current LF reading (Kalman: LF R=2%, PoR 5%, EF 10%) and are scored against LF at +travel time. That makes the Kalman essentially LF persistence with small nudges. Persistence-class models beat a GF estimate in quiet flow and lose on rises.
findings.evidence: DB SELECT shadow_leaderboard; data/snapshot-2026-11-10-gf.json shadowLeaderboard; scheduled-update.js lines 74-140, 530-690 and 1614-1660.
findings.recommendation: Snapshot the leaderboard daily or on a flow threshold. Add sum of squares so differences have uncertainty. Report shadows by flow state, not only lifetime. Label Kalman and onlineRegression as persistence-informed baselines.

findings.title: Post-mortem capability: most event evidence was lost to retention, deletion or never stored
findings.what_happened: Lost or never kept: (1) Clean validation rows, 7-day window: only 21 survive, because an earlier session captured them on 10-15 and 10-19. They lack raw, stages, flags and shadowModels. (2) Pending rows hold the whole input vector (LF, PoR, EF, tributaries, historic PoR, travel times) and are claim-deleted at validation, so no input vector survives for any event prediction, which is why the replay had to fit lags. (3) PoR history keeps 72 h and keeps the first-seen value only until trimmed, so original versus revised PoR is unrecoverable; the por_history row now spans 11-07 to 11-09. (4) gf_history keeps 24 h, so the graph line is gone. (5) Forecast rows are deleted after scoring and swept at 90 h, and forecast counters are driven by page views: +127 6-h-horizon scores in the 96 h after 10-15T16 against +136 in the next 21 days. (6) Bins are mutable with no history. (7) Soft-flag status is not stored on clean rows. (8) The validation_failure endpoint caps at 50 (currently back to 2026-07-10), but the DB keeps all 54, which reconciles with hardFlaggedValidations 54. October is safe. (9) waterTempC and gateVersion are absent from October failure rows. (10) The cumulative shadow and accuracy counters have no time series: avgErrorPercent moved only 7.379 to 7.3755 while hard flags rose 40 to 52.
findings.evidence: scheduled-update.js lines 348-390 (24 h), 434 (7 d), 303-330 (72 h), 1200-1245 (failure row fields); sync-learning.js lines 372 and 829 (limit 50); DB: validation_failure count 54, por_history span, gf_forecast_pending min created 2026-11-07; data/captured_context_2026-10.json forecast_accuracy_snapshots; NOTES.md (e).
findings.recommendation: Minimal additions: (a) an append-only gf_prediction_log row per stored prediction with the full input vector, the reading dateTimes and waterTempC, about 1 KB per hour; (b) an append-only per-validation row for clean rows, with raw, flags (soft and hard), stages and bin id; (c) a daily snapshot of all gf_correction_bin rows, the leaderboard and gf_metadata; (d) keep the first-seen PoR hourly value for 30 days; (e) write the forecast row's inputs and the NWS forecast at issue time.

findings.title: Pre-event bin states are partly reconstructable from created_at plus the clean-row list; the plan overstates flood contamination for bins at or above 25,000 cfs
findings.what_happened: gf_correction_bin created_at shows only 12000-25000/steady was born in the flood (2026-10-13T07:00:18, n=1, error 9,743 cfs, sumErrorSq equal to 9743 squared). 12000-25000 rising (05-24), falling (05-31) and all three 25000-50000 bins (05-25) pre-date it. The clean-row list gives the flood-time updates: 5 rising updates to 12000-25000 (10-12T15 to 10-14T06), so the 7 obs were about 2 pre-flood plus 5; 4-5 falling updates (10-15T00 to T12, maybe T16), so the 23 obs were about 18-19 pre-flood; and 2 falling updates to 25000-50000 (10-14T15, T18), so the 59 obs were about 97% pre-flood. The EMA values before the event are still unknown, and the 2 flood updates to 25000-50000 can move the EMA. Caveat: this assumes the 21 clean rows are every non-hard-flagged validation in the window.
findings.evidence: DB SELECT on gf_correction_bin (created_at and counts); data/captured_context_2026-10.json clean_validations (flowBin, flowState); NOTES.md (e).
findings.recommendation: Use these count bounds when bracketing the approx-corrected pass before 10-15T16. Do not describe the 25000-50000 bins as flood-learned. Treat the 12000-25000/steady n=1 bin (+9,743) as a fragile single-observation correction.

findings.title: PoR history retention always covered the time-shift lookup; the 3-step travel iteration often ends unconverged
findings.what_happened: Across the 313 replay ticks there were 0 null time-shift lookups. PoR-to-GF travel after iteration ran 7.2 to 45.4 h (max at 10-09T23 and 10-12T15). Stored history spanned 71.9 h. The minimum margin of span minus travel was 26.5 h. At the pre-event low flow (LF about 1,330-1,520) travel was 36-45 h. Nowcast estimator, component b.aspect: Nowcast estimator, component by component (raw model vs LF truth)
Nowcast estimator, component b.summary: I rebuilt the server estimator as a switchable copy. It reproduces the replay's raw value on all 313 ticks with a maximum difference of 0 cfs, so each ablation differs from production only by the one switch tested. Under the chosen lag setting the raw model scored MAPE/bias of 12.0/+11.0 pre-event, 46.0/-31.1 onset, 23.4/+23.2 rise, 11.4/+11.4 peak, 3.3/-3.0 early recession and 5.0/-4.9 late recession. This is one event, so these are observations rather than skill estimates. Recession was the model's best phase. The rise was its worst because of an internal mechanism. The travel-time lookback reaches back to pre-rise base flow, and the PoR-delta correction then scales the already-current tributary flows along with the PoR part. Applying the delta to the PoR part only would have cut rise MAPE from 23.4 to 13.6 and all-tick MAPE from 13.1 to 10.9. The same delta correction adds about 3.6 points of error in late recession. The +15%, 0, +15, 0 alternation comes from the 120%-of-LF ceiling combined with a validation horizon that swings between 3 and 9 hours. It is not a property of the estimator. The +18 to +37% peak errors come mainly from the PoR route, which carries no flood-wave attenuation and has too short a travel time at high flow. The Edwards Ferry law adds about 4 points on top of that. The EF law is wrong in a stage- and limb-dependent way. Measured tributaries are the largest single helper. The client's robust rise rate differs from the server's by at most 3.5% on this event. Component rankings hold at uniform lags L0 and L60 within about 2 to 3 points.

findings.title: Rise-limb over-read: travel lookback hits pre-rise base flow, then PoR-delta inflates PoR and tributaries together
findings.what_happened: On the rise (10-12T00 to 10-14T06, n=54) the raw model over-read by a mean of +23.2% (MAPE 23.4%). The cause is mechanical. The 3-step iteration starts from the low historic-PoR multiplier. On 10-13T05 to T14 it looked back 17.7 to 25.7 h at a PoR of about 2,900 to 3,000 cfs (base flow), and 22 of 54 rise ticks did not converge within 3 steps. Observed PoR to LF level-crossing lags on the rising limb were 6 to 15 h. The PoR-delta correction (cap 0.5) then patched the stale 3,000 cfs. It added a mean of +2,362 cfs on the PoR part and +3,253 cfs by multiplying the current tributary flow by the PoR ratio. That is 5.6k of the mean 15.2k raw. Mean truth over the phase was 12.3k. Counterfactuals: delta applied to the PoR part only gives rise 13.6/+3.5 and all ticks 10.9 vs 13.1. Delta off gives 19.4/-12.2. A fixed 9.4 h PoR to GF travel gives 16.0/+13.4. Fixed 9.4 h with a PoR-only delta gives 12.3/+6.8. The L0 and L60 inputs give the same ranking (PoR-only delta 13.7 and 13.4). Fidelity: no raw value was logged on the rising limb, so the raw level is unverified. What is verified is validation timing (41/41, including the 13 h and 16 h intervals that match the replayed long travel times), the cron LF view, and the 8 ceiling-bound rows. The 20 logged raw values elsewhere match within 1%.

findings.title: The +15, 0, +15, 0 alternation is the 120%-of-LF ceiling meeting a swinging validation horizon, not estimator behaviour
findings.what_happened: All 8 stored predictions from 10-12T02 to 10-14T09 were ceiling-bound, so the displayed value equals 1.2 times the cron's stale LF reading. The displayed error is therefore 1.2*LFc/LFv - 1, and the logged errors match this identity exactly (max deviation 0.00 pp). Error is about 0 when LF grows 20% or more over the validation interval, and about +15% when it grows about 4%. The interval alternates because validationDue uses the GF to LF travel time computed from the lagged historic-PoR multiplier. That travel time was 6.3 h, 8.6 h, 2.8 h and 3.2 h on the rows created 10-13T07, T14, T23 and 10-14T02. LF rose 11,000 to 11,300 (+2.7%, +16.8% error), 11,300 to 13,800 (+22%, -1.7%), 13,800 to 14,400 (+4.3%, +15.0%) and 14,400 to 17,400 (+21%, -0.7%). The ceiling hid a raw over-read: replay raw errors on those same 8 rows were +8% to +49% (median about +34%, rising-limb raw unverified). Over this stretch the displayed number carried no information from the PoR or EF model. It was LF persistence times 1.2, and the app's published accuracy for the rise reflects that.

findings.title: Peak over-read of +18 to +37% is the PoR route's missing attenuation and short travel time, with the EF law adding about 4 points; the logged +37% is also inflated by a 70-min-stale LF
findings.what_happened: For the 10-14T06 prediction the logged raw is 27,535 (replay 27,416) against the cron's stale LF 20,100 (+37%). Against physical LF at validationDue (20,937) it is +31%. For 10-14T09, 28,022 vs 23,600 is +18.7%. At 10-14T06 the PoR-based estimate was 26,649 (+27.3% vs truth), the EF law gave 28,581 (+36.5%), and the blend was +30.9%. So the EF law accounts for about 4 of the 31 points and the PoR route for the rest. Three things drive the PoR-route over-read. (1) The estimator has no flood-wave attenuation. findings.title: Edwards Ferry power law: good at 4.5 to 6.5 ft and on the falling limb, poor at low stage, on the rising limb and above 8.5 ft; the weight peaks exactly where it is worst
findings.what_happened: The ratio of EF-law flow to LF, aligned at the best lag (1 h), was: stage 2.5 to 3.5 ft, median 1.49 (n=88, range 0.80 to 1.67). Stage 4.5 to 5.5 ft, 0.97. Stage 5.5 to 6.5 ft, 0.96 on steady and falling, 1.125 rising. Stage 6.5 to 7.5 ft, 0.97 falling and 1.24 rising. Stage 7.5 to 8.5 ft, 1.04 falling and 1.50 rising. Stage 8.5 to 10 ft, 1.14 falling, 1.28 steady and 1.66 rising. At the EF stage peak (9.23 ft on 10-14T08) the law gives 29,838 cfs. That is 1.228 times the LF peak and 1.135 times the PoR peak. EF reaches its crest 6.8 h before LF, so the law's implied zero lag mismatches the rising limb. The logged 48% EF discrepancy compares 29,838 to the cron's LF of 20,100 (stale by 70 min). Against physical LF at that hour (23,600) the gap is 26%. Against the LF peak it is 23%. The logistic weight is 0.396 at 25k and 0.353 at 15k, so it is at its maximum in the stage range where the law over-reads. Effect of the blend: it helped the rise by 9.7 pp (partly by offsetting the PoR-delta over-read, see E1), hurt the peak by 3.8 pp, helped early recession by 2.2 pp, and was neutral pre-event because the weight is about 0. EF-only scored 16.8/+0.1 on the rise and 1.8/-1.3 in late recession, but 20.1/+20.1 at the peak and 49.3 pre-event. A hindsight best constant weight is 0.9 in the rise, 0.0 at the peak and 1.0 in late recession, which is unstable. Event refits (exponent 1.55 to 2.74) are not usable as a replacement because of hysteresis. The discrepancy guard (>50%) skipped EF on 11 onset ticks. Turning the guard off would improve the onset by 4.2 pp.
